title: Decisions on FBN Inbound-Shortage Reimbursement Cases
content:
*Reimbursement desk standard, Fulfilled by Northloop (FBN).*

**Scope.** This standard fixes the units the support desk approves when it decides a seller's open inbound-shortage case, the claim for units of an inbound shipment line that were never received; the approved units become the unit count of the case and the reimbursement run pays them afterwards.

**Conditions on the decision.**

- The units approved on an inbound shortage case are not fixed until the units claimed on that case equal the claimable shortage of its shipment line.
- An inbound shortage case is decided only after no warehouse-damage case of the same SKU opened before it still stands submitted.

Restated against the records: while the units claimed on the inbound-shortage case differ from the claimable shortage of its shipment line, its approved units are not yet fixed; and while any warehouse-damage case of the same SKU, opened before the inbound-shortage case, still stands submitted, the inbound-shortage case is not decided.

## Reading the second condition (hypothetical case lists for one SKU)

| Warehouse-damage cases of the same SKU | Opened | Status | Second condition met |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | | | yes |
| one | before the inbound-shortage case | approved | yes |
| one | before the inbound-shortage case | submitted | no |
| one | after the inbound-shortage case | submitted | yes |

## The decision tool

**Tool:** `approve_inbound_shortage_case_dfebd527` — a support-desk tool that the agent unlocks and then calls. One call marks the case approved and sets the unit count on the case to the units Northloop accepts for reimbursement, re-recording the loss kind, source references and SKU of the decision. The reimbursement payment is issued separately by Northloop's reimbursement run, not by this call.

### Parameters

- `case_id`: reference number of the seller's open FBN reimbursement case being decided, read from the seller's case list returned by the FBN case lookup.
- `reimbursement_type`: loss kind recorded on the case — `inbound_shortage` (an inbound shipment line received short), `lost_in_warehouse` (units missing inside a fulfillment center), `damaged_in_warehouse` (units damaged inside a fulfillment center), `customer_return_not_received` (a refunded buyer return that never arrived), `removal_lost` (a removal shipment to the seller lost) or `not_applicable` (a fee dispute rather than a loss claim).
- `adjustment_ref`: inventory adjustment reference the case names, copied from the case record; empty string when it names no single adjustment.
- `shipment_id`: inbound shipment number the case names, copied from the case record; empty string when it names none.
- `order_id`: marketplace order number the case names, copied from the case record; empty string when it names none.
- `removal_order_id`: removal order reference the case names, copied from the case record; empty string when it names none.
- `sku`: seller SKU of the case, copied character for character from the case record (verbatim).
- `units_approved`: units approved for reimbursement, a whole number of units, zero or more, with no fractional part.

### Return

A receipt with `case_id`, `sku`, `units_approved` (the units approved, now the case's unit count) and `case_status`, always `approved`. A returned receipt means the approval is recorded. No other outcome is defined.
